questions.prompt: The black puck carrier is driving toward the net. The gold defender has sprawled across the path to the net, reaching with an extended stick to take away the puck. What is the best read for the black puck carrier?
options: Protect the puck, cut around the sprawled defender, and attack the goalie one-on-one
Snap a quick shot now, before reading whether the lane is still there
Pull the puck to the backhand but stay in the same spot the defender is reaching into
Drive straight ahead into the defender to try to power through
questions.answer: Protect the puck, cut around the sprawled defender, and attack the goalie one-on-one
questions.explanation: The gold defender has committed his whole body to a desperation slide and cannot recover quickly. The best play is to protect the puck on the side away from his stick, cut around him, and take the goalie one-on-one. A rushed shot or staying in his reach lets the committed defender's stick still affect the play, when his commitment is actually the chance to beat him cleanly.

questions.prompt: The gold defender is lying on the ice with his stick reaching across the path to the net. True or False: the black player should shoot right into that spot where the defender is reaching.
options: True
False
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: Shooting into the spot where the defender is sprawled means firing right into his stick and body. The better play is to protect the puck and cut around him to get a clean look at the goalie.

questions.prompt: As the gold defender sprawls across the path, the black puck carrier slows down and tries to force a shot through him. What mistake is he making?
options: He is committing to the shot too early instead of reading the slide and cutting around
He is changing his angle so much that he loses the net
He is protecting the puck too tightly to get a shot off
He is skating so fast he cannot control the puck
questions.answer: He is committing to the shot too early instead of reading the slide and cutting around
questions.explanation: The defender has already thrown his whole body into the slide. Forcing a shot into him too early wastes the chance. The mistake is not using the defender's commitment against him by cutting around to attack the goalie cleanly.

questions.prompt: The black puck carrier protects the puck and cuts around the sprawled gold defender. What is he most likely to face next?
options: A one-on-one chance against the gold goalie in the crease
The gold goalie staying deep and giving up an empty corner of the net
The sprawled defender instantly back on his feet and in front again
No goalie at all, with a wide-open net
questions.answer: A one-on-one chance against the gold goalie in the crease
questions.explanation: Once he beats the sprawled defender, the only player left between him and the goal is the gold goalie in the crease. That is a one-on-one chance to finish. The goalie is there (not an empty net), and the defender who fully committed to the slide cannot pop back up instantly.

questions.prompt: The player in black has the puck 🏒. A player in gold is lying down on the ice to stop him. What should the black player do?
options: ✋ Stop and give the puck away
➡️ Skate around the player lying down and go to the net
questions.answer: ➡️ Skate around the player lying down and go to the net
questions.explanation: The gold player is down on the ice and cannot move fast. The black player should keep the puck safe, skate around him, and head to the net.

questions.prompt: The gold attacker has the puck in open ice and the black defender is skating in to challenge. What is the defender's best play here?
options: Angle the attacker toward the outside while keeping his stick on the puck
Skate straight at the puck and reach for it, opening up the middle
Back off and give the attacker more room to come at him
Turn his back to the attacker and coast away
questions.answer: Angle the attacker toward the outside while keeping his stick on the puck
questions.explanation: In a 1-on-1, the defender wants to close the gap under control, take away the middle, and steer the puck carrier to the outside while keeping an active stick on the puck. Reaching straight in opens the middle, and backing off or coasting away surrenders the contest.

questions.prompt: True or false: the gold player's stick is on the puck, so the black player is trying to take it away.
options: True
False
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The puck is on the ice along the gold player's stick, so the gold player is closest to it and the black player is the defender reaching in to take it away.

questions.prompt: Tap the player the black defender should be focused on stopping.
options: The gold attacker with the puck
The white boards behind the play
The blue line on the ice
questions.answer: The gold attacker with the puck
questions.explanation: With only the two skaters in frame, the defender's job is clear: pressure the gold puck carrier and contest possession. The boards and lines are reference points, not threats.

questions.prompt: Both sticks are reaching toward the puck between the two players. If the black defender keeps his stick on the puck and stays in front of the gold attacker, what is the most likely result?
options: The defender contests the puck and can force a turnover or steer the attacker to the outside
The gold attacker protects the puck and cuts back to the middle past the defender
The puck squirts loose to open ice and becomes a 50/50 race
Both players skate away from the puck
questions.answer: The defender contests the puck and can force a turnover or steer the attacker to the outside
questions.explanation: Keeping an active stick on the puck and staying in good defensive position lets the defender win the battle or push the attacker to the outside. There is no net or goalie in frame, so this is about winning the open-ice contest, not stopping a shot.

questions.prompt: Whose stick is on the puck right now? 🏒
options: ⬛ black player
🟨 gold player
questions.answer: 🟨 gold player
questions.explanation: The puck is by the gold player's stick, so the gold player is closest to it and the black player is trying to get it.

questions.prompt: It's a 1-on-1 near the boards. The gold player is reaching for the loose puck and the black defender is arriving. What is the black defender's best move?
options: Angle the gold player toward the boards while closing the gap to challenge the puck
Reach in with the stick for the puck without closing the gap or angling
Skate straight at the puck head-on, giving the gold player an easy escape lane
Turn his back to the gold player and coast away
questions.answer: Angle the gold player toward the boards while closing the gap to challenge the puck
questions.explanation: The black defender should use angling and gap control to steer the gold player into the boards, taking away time and space and giving himself the best chance to win the loose puck. Reaching in without closing, or skating straight at the puck, both leave the gold player an easy lane to escape.

questions.prompt: True or false: In this loose-puck battle near the boards, the gold player already has full control of the puck on his stick.
options: True
False
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: The puck is loose on the ice and the gold player is still reaching for it. Nobody has it yet, so both players can still win it.

questions.prompt: Tap the loose puck both players are battling to win.
options: The loose puck on the ice near the bottom-center, between the two players
The gold player's stick blade
The black player's skates
The boards behind the players
questions.answer: The loose puck on the ice near the bottom-center, between the two players
questions.explanation: The puck is sitting loose on the ice near the bottom-center, with the gold player's stick extended toward it. The sticks, skates, and boards are part of the scene, but winning that loose puck is what the whole battle is about.

questions.prompt: The black defender keeps closing and angles the gold player toward the boards as the gold player reaches for the loose puck. What is the most likely next outcome?
options: The black defender seals the gold player against the boards and the two battle for possession of the puck
The gold player chips the loose puck past the defender and regains it cleanly in open ice
The puck squirts loose off both sticks and slides along the boards as the battle resets
The gold player skates away untouched into open ice with the puck
questions.answer: The black defender seals the gold player against the boards and the two battle for possession of the puck
questions.explanation: With the defender angling and the puck still loose, the play funnels toward the boards into a body-and-stick battle for the puck. The other outcomes are physically possible moments but less likely once the defender has closed the gap and taken away the escape lane; this becomes a contained 1-on-1 contest.

questions.prompt: Two players are racing for the loose puck by the boards. What should the black player do? 🏒
options: Skate hard and try to get the puck first 💨
Stop and sit down 🛑
Skate to the bench 🚪
questions.answer: Skate hard and try to get the puck first 💨
questions.explanation: When the puck is loose, the black player should hustle and skate hard to reach it before the gold player. Winning the race to the puck is how you win the battle.

questions.prompt: The black puck carrier is skating in alone on the gold goalie with no defenders in the way. What is the best read right now?
options: Attack the net and choose to shoot or deke the goalie
Stop and wait for a teammate to catch up
Pass the puck back behind the carrier
Skate the puck into the corner
questions.answer: Attack the net and choose to shoot or deke the goalie
questions.explanation: The black puck carrier is alone on the gold goalie with no defenders between them, which is a breakaway. The best play is to drive in and beat the goalie by shooting or deking. There is no teammate in frame to wait for or pass to.

questions.prompt: True or False: With the gold goalie set and the carrier still a way out, the black puck carrier should keep skating in to cut down the angle before deciding to shoot or deke, rather than firing right away from far out.
options: True
False
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: On a breakaway a far-out shot gives the set goalie an easy save. The carrier should keep attacking to close the distance and tighten the angle, then choose to shoot or deke at a better range. There are no defenders in frame to force a rushed shot.

questions.prompt: Tap the player the black puck carrier has to beat to score.
options: The gold goalie in the crease
The empty net behind the goalie
The open ice to the goalie's side
The puck on the carrier's stick
questions.answer: The gold goalie in the crease
questions.explanation: The only player between the black puck carrier and the net is the gold goalie set in the crease, so the carrier must beat the goalie to score. The net, the open ice, and the puck are things in the scene but none of them is the player you have to beat.

questions.prompt: The black puck carrier is skating in alone with the puck toward the gold goalie. What happens next if the carrier makes a good play?
options: The carrier drives in and shoots or dekes to try to score
The carrier passes to a teammate by the net
A defender steps in and steals the puck
The carrier turns around and skates away from the net
questions.answer: The carrier drives in and shoots or dekes to try to score
questions.explanation: On a breakaway the carrier keeps attacking the gold goalie and tries to score by shooting or deking. There is no teammate to pass to and no defender in frame to steal the puck.

questions.prompt: The black player has the puck 🏒 and is skating at the goalie 🥅 all alone. What should the black player do? 😀
options: Skate at the net and try to score 🚀
Stop and sit down 🛑
Skate away from the net ⬅️
questions.answer: Skate at the net and try to score 🚀
questions.explanation: The black player has the puck all alone with just the goalie to beat. The fun, correct play is to skate right at the net and try to score.

questions.prompt: The referee is leaning in to drop the puck between the black player and the gold player. What should the black player do to win this faceoff?
options: Stand up straight and wait to see where the puck goes
Stay low with the stick down and pull the puck back the instant it drops
Skate away from the dot before the drop
Drop the stick and use the body only
questions.answer: Stay low with the stick down and pull the puck back the instant it drops
questions.explanation: Both players are crouched with sticks down on the ice. A quick, low first move on the drop is how you win the draw.

questions.prompt: True or false: the black player and the gold player both have their sticks down on the ice, ready for the referee to drop the puck.
options: True
False
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: In the image both faceoff players are crouched with their stick blades down near the puck location as the referee prepares to drop it.

questions.prompt: If the gold player stood up tall and lifted the stick off the ice right before the referee dropped the puck, what is the mistake?
options: Nothing, that is the correct way to take a faceoff
Losing the low ready stance means a slower first move, so the opponent likely wins the draw
Standing tall gives a better view of the puck, so it actually helps win the draw
It would force the referee to skate away
questions.answer: Losing the low ready stance means a slower first move, so the opponent likely wins the draw
questions.explanation: Both players need to stay low with the stick on the ice. Standing up and lifting the stick removes the quick reaction needed to win the puck on the drop, and a slightly better view does not make up for the lost first move.

questions.prompt: The referee drops the puck. The gold player reacts a split second faster and gets a stick on it first. What most likely happens next?
options: The gold player pulls the puck to their side and gains control
The black player still gets possession because they are bigger
The black player ties up the gold player's stick and the puck stays loose in the dot
The black player is awarded the puck automatically
questions.answer: The gold player pulls the puck to their side and gains control
questions.explanation: Whoever wins the draw with the quicker first move on the drop directs the puck to their own side and gains possession. Size alone does not decide it, and the puck is not awarded automatically.

questions.prompt: The black-and-white striped referee is about to drop the puck for a faceoff. What do the two players do? 🏒⬇️
options: 😴 Take a nap
👀⚡ Watch the puck and get it fast
🙈 Close their eyes
questions.answer: 👀⚡ Watch the puck and get it fast
questions.explanation: On a faceoff both players watch the puck and try to get it quickly when the referee drops it.

questions.prompt: The black puck carrier is turning while the gold defender skates in and reaches with the stick. What is the best read for the black player right now?
options: Protect the puck by keeping the body between the puck and the gold defender's stick
Stickhandle through the defender's reaching stick on the open side
Skate straight at the gold defender to try to push past
Turn the back all the way to the defender so the puck is behind the body and out of sight
questions.answer: Protect the puck by keeping the body between the puck and the gold defender's stick
questions.explanation: The gold defender is reaching in with the stick, so the black puck carrier protects possession by keeping the body between the defender and the puck while continuing to move. Stickhandling through the reaching stick exposes the puck, charging straight at the defender invites the check, and over-rotating so the puck is out of sight costs both protection and vision.

questions.prompt: True or false: The gold defender is skating in and extending the stick toward the puck carrier to challenge for the puck.
options: True
False
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The gold defender is skating toward the black puck carrier and extending the stick to challenge for the puck. That is a stick check / containment attempt in a 1-on-1.

questions.prompt: Tap the player who has the puck.
options: The black player (left)
The gold player (right)
questions.answer: The black player (left)
questions.explanation: The black player on the left is controlling the puck with the stick low to the ice. The gold player on the right has no puck and is defending.

questions.prompt: The gold defender is closing in and reaching with the stick as the black puck carrier turns. What is the most likely next moment?
options: The black puck carrier uses the turn and body to shield the puck away from the reaching gold stick
The gold defender pokes the puck loose because the black player exposes it
The black player stops the turn early and the gold stick reaches the puck
Both players stop and leave the puck still
questions.answer: The black puck carrier uses the turn and body to shield the puck away from the reaching gold stick
questions.explanation: With the gold defender reaching in, the black puck carrier's turn naturally continues into shielding the puck on the far side of the body. The defender only wins the puck if the black player exposes it or stops the turn early; players stopping and leaving the puck still is not realistic in a live 1-on-1.

questions.prompt: Who has the puck? ⚫ black player or 🟡 gold player?
options: ⚫ black player
🟡 gold player
questions.answer: ⚫ black player
questions.explanation: The black player is keeping the puck on the stick. The gold player is chasing to get it.

questions.prompt: The mostly-black player and the gold player are leaning shoulder-to-shoulder in the corner, both reaching their sticks toward a loose puck on the ice. What decides who wins this battle?
options: Winning inside body position to protect and reach the puck first
Swinging your stick at the puck as hard as you can without sealing the opponent off
Letting go of your stick to push the opponent with both hands
Skating away from the puck to wait for a teammate
questions.answer: Winning inside body position to protect and reach the puck first
questions.explanation: This is a 50-50 corner battle. With both players contesting a loose puck along the boards, the one who establishes the inside body position can shield the opponent off and get to the puck first. Just swinging at the puck or pushing with two hands surrenders position. No passing option is visible in this frame, so the read is to win the wall.

questions.prompt: True or False: One team already has clear possession of the puck in this picture.
options: True
False
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: The puck is loose on the ice between the two players' skates, and neither the black nor the gold player controls it. It is a 50-50 puck, so both players are still battling to win it.

questions.prompt: Tap the thing both players are fighting to win in this corner battle.
options: The loose puck on the ice
The boards behind them
A teammate
The net
questions.answer: The loose puck on the ice
questions.explanation: Both the black and gold players have their sticks lowered toward the loose puck on the ice. That puck is the prize of the board battle. There is no net or teammate visible in this frame, so the only correct target is the loose puck.

questions.prompt: If the gold player turned away from the black player and bent over the puck, reaching for it without sealing the opponent off, what mistake would that be?
options: Giving up body position and letting the opponent pin or steal the puck
Protecting the puck better than before
A smart way to pass to a teammate
The correct way to win every board battle
questions.answer: Giving up body position and letting the opponent pin or steal the puck
questions.explanation: In a shoulder-to-shoulder corner battle, staying square and keeping your body between the opponent and the puck is what wins it. Turning away to reach for the puck surrenders inside position and lets the black player lean in, pin the gold player, and take the loose puck.

questions.prompt: Two players are pushing for the puck by the wall. What should you do? 💪🏒
options: Be strong, get in front 💪
Skate away 🙈
Sit down 😴
questions.answer: Be strong, get in front 💪
questions.explanation: When two players battle for a loose puck by the boards, the one who gets strong and puts their body in the way wins it. Be brave, lean in, and reach for the puck.

shippable.archetype: net drive / slot scoring chance (one attacker vs goalie + collapsing defenders)

questions.prompt: The black player has the puck in the slot, skating toward the goal. The gold goalie is set in the crease and two gold defenders are positioned on either side of him. What is the best play?
options: Attack the net himself and take a quality shot or drive before the defenders collapse
Force a cross-ice pass into traffic
Try to deke around both defenders into the corner
Stop and wait in the slot for help to arrive
questions.answer: Attack the net himself and take a quality shot or drive before the defenders collapse
questions.explanation: The black puck carrier is in the slot with two gold defenders ready to collapse and no support showing. His best option is to take the scoring chance himself, drive the net and get a quality shot, before the defenders close the lane or strip the puck. Forcing a pass into traffic or over-handling the puck just gives the defenders time to collapse.

questions.prompt: True or False: Because the gold goalie is square and set facing the shooter, driving wide for a better shooting angle can be smarter than firing straight into the goalie's chest.
options: True
False
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The goalie is set and square to the black puck carrier. Shooting straight at a set goalie is a low-percentage play, so changing the angle by driving wide can open up more net to shoot at.

questions.prompt: Tap the player who has the puck and is in the best spot to score right now.
options: The black player in the slot facing the net
The gold goalie in the crease
The gold defender on the left
The gold defender on the right
questions.answer: The black player in the slot facing the net
questions.explanation: The black player has the puck in the slot, right in front of the net and facing the goal. That is the most dangerous scoring spot on the ice, so he is the one in position to score.

questions.prompt: The black puck carrier is in the slot with two gold defenders on either side and the gold goalie set. If he hesitates and tries to wait for a play to develop, what is the most likely outcome?
options: The two gold defenders collapse and take the puck or block the shooting lane
He gets a clean look once both defenders commit to the goalie
The defenders back off and leave him open
The goalie skates out of the crease to give him more room
questions.answer: The two gold defenders collapse and take the puck or block the shooting lane
questions.explanation: Both gold defenders are positioned on either side of the slot, ready to close in. The longer the black player waits, the more time they have to collapse on him, strip the puck, or block his shot. That is why attacking quickly or protecting the puck is the better read.

questions.prompt: The black player has the puck right in front of the net. What should he try to do? 🏒🥅
options: Shoot at the net! 🥅
Skate away from the net ⬅️
Sit down on the ice 🪑
Give the puck to the other team 🧤
questions.answer: Shoot at the net! 🥅
questions.explanation: The black player has the puck close to the net, so the fun and smart thing to do is shoot and try to score!

shippable.archetype: breakaway / scoring chance — attacker driving the net one-on-one against the goalie

questions.prompt: The black puck carrier is driving in alone on the gold goalie with no defender between them. What is the best play here?
options: Read the set goalie and decide whether to shoot or deke as he closes in
Fire a slap shot from far out before he gets close to the goalie
Slow down and deke without ever looking up at the goalie
Cut wide and skate the puck behind the net
questions.answer: Read the set goalie and decide whether to shoot or deke as he closes in
questions.explanation: With the puck out front and no defender visible, the black carrier has a clean breakaway. His job is to read the set gold goalie and pick shoot or deke as he gets close. Shooting from far out is easy to stop, deking blind takes his eyes off the goalie, and cutting behind the net throws the chance away.

questions.prompt: True or false: the black puck carrier has a clear lane to the net and only the gold goalie left to beat.
options: True
False
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: No defender is visible between the carrier and the net, so his path is open. The only obstacle left is the set gold goalie, which is exactly what makes this a breakaway.

questions.prompt: The black puck carrier is closing in on the set gold goalie with the puck out front. What happens next if he makes a strong move?
options: He shoots or dekes to try to beat the gold goalie and score
He shoots from too far out and the goalie covers it easily
He skates wide and runs out of room behind the net
He turns around and skates back to his own end
questions.answer: He shoots or dekes to try to beat the gold goalie and score
questions.explanation: On a breakaway the carrier finishes the chance. As he reaches the gold goalie he shoots or dekes to get the puck past him into the net. Shooting too early, skating too wide, or turning back all give up the scoring chance.

questions.prompt: The black puck carrier is on a breakaway against the gold goalie. Which of these would be a mistake on this rush?
options: Keeping his eyes down on the puck instead of reading the goalie
Keeping his head up to watch how the goalie moves
Carrying the puck out in front where he can shoot or deke
Picking up speed as he drives toward the net
questions.answer: Keeping his eyes down on the puck instead of reading the goalie
questions.explanation: On a breakaway the carrier needs his eyes up to read the set gold goalie and choose shoot or deke. Watching the puck the whole way lets the goalie square up and take the chance away. Head up, puck out front, and good speed are all the right habits.

questions.prompt: The black player has the puck and is skating right at the goalie all by himself. What should he try to do? 🏒
options: 🥅 Skate at the goalie and try to score
🔄 Pass it to a friend even though no one is there
↩️ Turn around and skate away from the net
questions.answer: 🥅 Skate at the goalie and try to score
questions.explanation: The black player has the puck all alone near the net. When you are by yourself, take it yourself! Skate at the goalie and try to score. 🎉
